ambiguities.evidence: The paper says only that inequality (7) 'can be adapted' for mappings satisfying equation (10), without displaying the adapted condition. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, paragraph containing eq. (10))
ambiguities.impact: No exact generalized FastTwoSum precondition may be reconstructed from this passage alone; only equation (10) itself has a precise contract. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, eq. (10) discussion)
ambiguities.issue: The claimed adaptation beyond nearest-addition is not specified quantitatively. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, sentence following eq. (10))

ambiguities.evidence: The definition requires minimum absolute distance but gives no tie-breaking convention. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, nearest-addition definition)
ambiguities.impact: A formalization may choose any nearest result in a tie, but equation (10) must hold for that choice. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, nearest-addition definition; PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, eq. (10))
ambiguities.issue: Nearest-rounding ties are left unspecified. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, nearest-rounding definition)

contract_plain_english: For floating-point x and y, a nearest evaluation of x+y is no farther from the exact sum than the already representable candidate x, so its absolute error is at most |y|. This is only an addition-error bound; the passage does not by itself claim an error-free FastTwoSum decomposition. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, eq. (9); PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, eq. (10))

source_evidence.observation: A nearest-addition maps x,y in F to a floating-point number whose absolute distance from the exact real sum x+y is minimal among all members of F.
For s=x⊕y, nearest-addition and the admissible candidate x in F give |s-(x+y)|=min_{f in F}|f-(x+y)|≤|x-(x+y)|=|y|.
The paper isolates |x⊕y-(x+y)|≤|y| as the only property of nearest-addition used in the proof of Theorem 2.

statement.algorithm_linkage: This contract concerns only the computed addition s=x⊕y in FastTwoSum. By itself, equation (10) does not assert that the remaining FastTwoSum operations are exact or that an error-free decomposition is produced. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, FastTwoSum algorithm; PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, eq. (10) discussion)
binders: For every pair of scalar floating-point values x,y in F and an operation ⊕:F×F→F, let s=x⊕y be the computed addition result. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, nearest-addition definition; PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, eq. (10))
F is the fixed-base floating-point set F={m beta^e : m,e integers, -beta^p<m<beta^p, e_min≤e≤e_max}. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, eq. (1))
conclusions: The computed addition obeys the non-strict absolute-error bound |x⊕y-(x+y)|≤|y|. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, eq. (10); derivation in PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, eq. (9))

The paper additionally says that for any mapping ⊕:F×F→F satisfying this bound, condition (7) can be adapted so that the FastTwoSum identity (3) remains valid; it does not state the adapted inequality. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, paragraph containing eq. (10))
constants_and_indexing: The coefficient multiplying |y| is exactly 1 and the inequality is inclusive. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, eq. (10))
The bound is operand-order-sensitive as written: it uses the second operand y, not a symmetric expression or an indexed collection. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, eq. (10))
definitions_and_conventions: The expression x+y is exact real addition, whereas x⊕y is its floating-point approximation in F. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, operation model preceding the nearest-addition definition)
The bound follows by comparing the nearest result with the particular candidate f=x, whose error from x+y is exactly |y|. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, eq. (9))
error_notions: The error is the scalar forward error between the computed floating-point sum and the exact real sum. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, eq. (10))
Equation (10) bounds the magnitude of the error but does not itself assert that the signed residual x+y-(x⊕y) belongs to F. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, eq. (10) and following discussion)
exceptional_values: The model F contains finite real values, including zero, and does not model infinities, NaNs, or distinct signed zeros. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, eq. (1))
No separate underflow or overflow exclusion is attached to equation (10) in the abstract nearest-member model fl:R→F. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, rounding model; PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, eq. (10))
higher_order_terms: Equation (10) is an exact finite inequality with no big-O term, omitted higher-order term, or unit-roundoff expansion. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, eq. (10))
hypotheses: The operation ⊕ is nearest-addition, meaning its result minimizes absolute distance to the exact real sum over all f in F. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, nearest-addition definition)
implicit_context: Equation (10) itself requires no exponent ordering, magnitude ordering, or hypothesis (7). (PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, eq. (10))
Equation (10) is used for line 1 of the original FastTwoSum procedure, where s=x⊕y. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, FastTwoSum line 1; PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, discussion of eq. (10))
norms: Only the ordinary absolute value on scalar real numbers is used; no vector or matrix norm appears. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, eq. (9); PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, eq. (10))
numerical_model: Rounding is to a nearest member of F; no tie-breaking rule is specified. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, standing rounding-to-nearest assumption)

Faithful rounding alone does not necessarily imply equation (10); the paper gives the case where y is smaller than half the distance from x to its nearest neighbor but the faithfully rounded sum is not x. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, paragraph following eq. (10))

undebatable_constraints: The exact source inequality is |x⊕y-(x+y)|≤|y|. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, eq. (10))
The computed quantity is x⊕y and the reference quantity is the exact real sum x+y. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, operation model; PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, eq. (10))
Nearest-addition is sufficient because x itself is a candidate in F. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, eq. (9))
Faithful-addition without further conditions is not sufficient for equation (10). (PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, paragraph following eq. (10))
The passage does not replace |y| with |x|, min{|x|,|y|}, a relative error, or an ulp bound. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, eq. (10))
